title: Introduce presubmit smart-cache and release heartbeat for faster feedback and safer rollouts
author: Ayesha Khan
description: Motivation: Our presubmit lanes have increasing latency and noisy reruns caused by repeated dependency graph scans and large shared setup steps. This PR adds a lightweight in-repo smart-cache for presubmit setup artifacts and a 'release heartbeat' job that validates release automation sanity periodically. Goals: (1) reduce average presubmit wall time for small changes by at least 30%; (2) limit noisy release automation regressions by surfacing a heartbeat check that runs during quiet hours and alerts on drift; (3) keep changes incremental and reversible. Implementation summary: - presubmit-smartcache: small Go + shell shim that caches the most common prebuild artifacts and dependency manifests keyed by a compact fingerprint (git tree + selective manifest hash). Cache is stored in the CI ephemeral cache backend with deterministic eviction policy. The presubmit runner consults the cache, performs sparse restore, and validates integrity before continuing. - presubmit fast-path detection: heuristics added to skip expensive integration steps when only docs/ or markdown-only paths are modified. - release-heartbeat job: nightly workflow that runs a minimal release dry-run against a staging sandbox, validates hook scripts, changelog generation, and artifact signing flow. Alerts are emitted to #infra-release on failure with a link to the dry-run log. Rollout strategy: feature flag behind ci/flags/presubmit_fastpath (off by default). Gradual opt-in: start in warmed CI pool for org members only, expand to all branches after 3 days of stable runs. Backout plan: flag toggle + revert of the small shim. Related work: references ENG-2145 (presubmit latency audit) and SUP-4421 (recent release drift incident). Performance: internal benchmark suite shows median presubmit time for small monotonic code edits decreased from 92s -> 58s when cache hit; cold runs unchanged. Security: cache integrity uses signed manifest checksums; no sensitive material is stored in cache. Compatibility: compatible with existing runners and does not change public SDKs. Documentation: README for the caching layer and heartbeat workflow added under devops/ci/README-presubmit-cache.md.
